ten_year.rationale: The US ten-year at 4.85 is down 22bp over five sessions and 6bp yesterday, and Australia and Japan ten-years fell with it. That is the cash rally that is still extending.

two_year.rationale: The US two-year at 4.61 is down 19bp over five sessions but only 2bp yesterday, so the front-end cash rally is no longer extending as cleanly as the ten-year.

expression_memo.rationale: The ten-year rally extended yesterday, while the Australian dollar bounced and the other dollar pairs are stalled or back inside a failed break.

spot_candidate.rationale: Short Australian dollar would ride the monthly decline, but yesterday was up 1 percent and the one-year z-score is already -2.05, so a new short would sell a bounce inside an extreme.

lifecycle.realization_logic: The receive is marked on the ten-year yield and profits while that yield keeps falling with the five-day rally in global cash yields.

causal.assumptions_right: The entry alignment was real: March, the two-year, and the ten-year were higher together when the pay was opened. The invalidation correctly named a split between March and the cash curve as the cover.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The pay assumed the higher-yield alignment would persist past the entry day. It underweighted how fast the ten-year could fall while March only slipped.
causal.causal_divergence: The ten-year decline over five sessions broke the joint rise the pay required. March did not keep rising with the cash curve, so the written cover was that divergence.
causal.future_implication: A later receive belongs in the cash tenor that is still making lower yields, which is now the ten-year. Paying March again would fight the five-day decline in cash yields.
causal.observed_reality: By the 25 November close, March had stopped rising with the cash curve and the ten-year had fallen over five sessions without a new yield high. The stored result on the closed pay is a small loss rather than a continued rise.
causal.original_belief: The March pay was opened because the implied rate was rising with the two-year and the ten-year. The position was meant to profit only while that joint rise continued.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the ten-year already down and March off the entry, keeping the pay would have held a contract that had stopped confirming. Covering, and not replacing it with a new short, is what that information required.

postmortems.expression_assessment: March stopped confirming the cash curve. There was no cash tenor still making new yield highs to rotate a pay into, and closing rather than re-shorting was the rule.
postmortems.no_new_lesson: The cover followed the written invalidation once March stopped rising together with the two-year and the ten-year, so the original process remains sound. The small giveback on the closed pay is bounded variance inside that rule.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The entry was aligned when March, the two-year, and the ten-year were higher together. The thesis required that joint rise to continue, and the cover followed the rule once the ten-year had rolled over.
postmortems.what_failed: March implied slipped while the ten-year fell over five sessions and did not make a new high. The joint rise that the pay required had already ended, so the position was no longer a live higher-yield trend.
postmortems.what_worked: The March pay was covered once the ten-year had rolled over and had not printed a new high. That was the written cover for a pay that was no longer rising with the cash curve.

causal.assumptions_right: Crude did not reprice into the scare named at entry, so oil did not make 1.43 fair. Brent at 94.61 still supports Canada and was never the invalidation.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The close treated a still-pinned 1.43 as a finished convergence three sessions into a twenty-session test. The later 1.423 print was underweighted as residual richness rather than as evidence the closed ticket had not been paid.
causal.causal_divergence: The belief required either a lower dollar-Canada inside the horizon or a completed pin test, and the close delivered neither. Price left the pin only after the book was flat, and 1.423 with a z-score of 1.60 is not the convergence the entry described.
causal.future_implication: Do not reload dollar-Canada just because 1.423 is still a z-score of 1.60. The 1.43 pin is gone, Brent at 94.61 still sponsors Canada, and any new short needs its own anchor rather than this ticket.
causal.observed_reality: The ticket closed on 23 November after about three sessions, with the pair still at the pin. Live dollar-Canada is 1.423, still a one-year z-score of 1.60, while Brent is 94.61 and WTI is 83.68, neither a print above 100.
causal.original_belief: Dollar-Canada entered near 1.43004 was rich on the one-year screen, and crude was not a scare that made 1.43 fair. The short was meant to stay until the pair converged or until it remained pinned at or above 1.43004 for about twenty sessions.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the same entry near 1.43004, the same non-scare oil tape, and the same invalidation, the short remains open while the pair is still at the pin. It is closed only after about twenty pinned sessions or after crude reprices to a scare that makes 1.43 fair.

postmortems.expression_assessment: Spot was the right place for that valuation short, because a two-year Canada rates spread is not cheap merely because dollar-Canada looks rich. The miss was leaving the spot short early, not the choice of spot.
postmortems.future_rule: Keep a dollar-Canada valuation short through the stated session count unless crude reprices to the scare written at entry. Do not treat a same-mark exit, or a later residual z-score, as proof the original convergence already occurred.
postmortems.lesson: An unchanged 1.43 round trip closed before the written pin horizon is an unfinished valuation test, not a captured convergence. The later move to 1.423 belongs to a new question and does not reopen the closed short by itself.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The rich dollar-Canada thesis was not falsified, because crude never made 1.43 fair and the pair did not complete a twenty-session pin. Closing at an unchanged mark ended the test while the one-year z-score was still positive.
postmortems.timing_assessment: Three sessions against a written horizon of about twenty sessions is an early exit, not a completed horizon. On 23 November both the pin test and the crude-scare test were still open.
postmortems.what_failed: The exit was the same 1.43 mark as the booked entry, about three sessions in, so the book left before the twenty-session pin test. The later live level of 1.423 was the direction of the short and was not this ticket.
postmortems.what_worked: Oil behaved as the thesis required. Brent at 94.61 and WTI at 83.68 stayed short of a three-digit scare, so the short was not invalidated by crude. The entry screen was a real richness near 1.43.
